messages:
maria: Heads-up idea — I want to try a 'graceful fallback lanes' pattern for our spot GPU pools. Instead of a flat mixed-instance group, split into primary low-evict/high-perf lane and secondary high-diversity low-cost lane that keeps a lightweight inference path live when primaries are reclaimed.

kai: can you sketch how requests get routed? curious about binpacking impact and memory fragmentation.

maria: routing: requests prefer primary lane instances. on eviction events we shift a small % of new requests to secondary lane where we run smaller model variants or sharded fragments. goal is keep P95 under SLA while saving money. eviction handler toggles routing weight.

shreya: looks promising. two quick concerns: 1) binpacking — mixing many instance types in secondary can worsen fragmentation for big jobs, 2) network locality for KV cache when we fallback.

maria: agree. plan is: pack large, latency-sensitive pods on the primary lane with binpack affinity; secondary lane lets us spread smaller replicas across many instance types. we also keep a tiny in-memory KV cache replica on secondary instances (subset) to reduce cross-AZ reads.

kai: example affinity config?

shreya: here's a rough pod spec fragment we used in the last experiment:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  labels:
    rl-qos: primary
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    pool: gpu-primary
  topologySpreadConstraints:
  - maxSkew: 1
    topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
    whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu-priority"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "primary"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```

shreya: secondary pods use `pool: gpu-secondary` and an admission hook sets model-size to "micro" for fallback images.

david: what's the cost delta and expected hit to throughput? also watch out for cross-az egress for KV sync (that can blow cost and latency).

maria: cost delta target: +35–50% spot coverage (vs current ~20%) saving ~18% on GPU spend in prelim calc. throughput hit depends on how many requests are allowed to fallback; initial experiment will cap fallback at 5% of new requests, ramp to 20% if stable.

kai: how do we detect eviction quickly and change routing? cloud provider spot events lag.

maria: two signals fused: provider interruption webhook + node kubelet eviction taint + our runtime observed token-drop in KV RPCs. we reacted to taint in last test in ~9s. routing toggles via a small feature-flag service that updates Envoy weights for the route.

shreya: we should also compress model checkpoints and use on-node lazy-load to reduce startup time when secondary needs to serve heavier queries. lazy-load reduces cold-start tail.

maria: yep — plan includes: quantize fallback images, eager prefetch of top-10 prompts, and keep shard metadata warm in local SSD.

ops-bot: autoscaler: scaleGroup gpu-secondary down 6 -> 4 (reason: spot reclaim)

david: can we run a canary in eu-west-1 first? network latency and pricing differ a lot there.

maria: good call. I'll open a canary targeting eu-west-1 and us-central-1 simultaneously to compare eviction profiles and egress costs. metric list: P50/P95 latency, tail cold-start, eviction rate, cross-AZ egress bytes, cost per 1k tokens.

kai: add a success criteria: keep P95 < 220ms on primary+fallback combined, rollback if cross-AZ egress > 2x baseline.

maria: noted. I'll draft the runbook and the rollout knob (percent fallback) and post here. starting experiment tomorrow morning. :rocket:

shreya: thanks — if you want I can help with the scheduler tweaks and packing heuristics.

maria: please do. pinging @shreya for follow-up pairing.

ops-bot: incident: spotPriceSpike alert on eu-west-1 (past 15m) — observed for instance family a100.

maria: perfect timing, that's the exact signal we want to exercise. I'll correlate logs and post results.
